output.question: Has The Washington Post announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. The most recent announcement came on October 7, 2026, when the Post told state and local officials it would lay off 118 workers as it closes its Springfield, Virginia printing plant. Those layoffs take effect December 31, 2026. The company says it is moving its print operations to a new facility on the Dulles Toll Road by January 2027, not shutting them down. Earlier, on February 4, 2026, the Post made much larger cuts, laying off about one-third of its staff and reducing coverage across sports, books, editing, metro and international news, including several foreign bureaus.

key_facts.fact: On Oct. 7, 2026, the Post notified state and local officials of layoffs affecting 118 workers, tied to closing its Springfield, VA printing plant.
The printing plant layoffs are scheduled to take effect Dec. 31, 2026.
A Post spokesperson said the company is relocating print operations to a new Dulles Toll Road facility by January 2027, not shutting them down.
On Feb. 4, 2026, the Post laid off about one-third of its staff. Cuts hit sports, books, editing, metro and international coverage, and several foreign bureaus were closed.

passages.quote: on track to complete relocation to our new print facility on Dulles Toll Road by January 2027
cuts apply to about one-third of newsroom
difficult but decisive actions today for our future
sport, books, editing, metro, and international coverage

caveats: Sources disagree on the scale of the February 2026 cuts. Some describe one-third of all staff, others about one-third of the newsroom. Search results also cited 300+ of roughly 800 newsroom employees (Britannica), but I did not open that page to confirm.

Search snippets said about half of Springfield staff may move to the Dulles site, and that publisher and CEO Will Lewis stepped down days after the February layoffs. I did not confirm either point on a page I opened.
I could not open the Post's own WARN filing or any statement from the company itself. The October figures come from local news reports (FFXnow; also reported by WUSA9 and Virginia Business).
I found no reports of new cuts after mid-October 2026, but more recent announcements may not be indexed yet.
